messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden spike in 503s for hosted inference (us-west-2) over last 2m. p95 error rate up ~18%. routing shows upstream worker exits on runner pool. creating thread for triage.
deploy-bot: NOTE: quant-swap-v2 rollout to us-west-2-worker-pool started @ 2026-03-18T14:50:12 (50% traffic).
ali: seeing multiple customer escalations (CS-4123, CS-4128). symptoms: 503 gateway errors and occasional 500. customers report long streaming requests time out. :frowning:
maria: pulled recent runner logs from pod infer-runner-7a4bf:
```
2026-03-18T15:02:31Z infer-runner[2312]: ERROR kernel_attn.cu: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
2026-03-18T15:02:31Z infer-runner[2312]: cuda runtime error: out of memory at allocate
2026-03-18T15:02:31Z infer-runner[2312]: Backtrace:
  #0 0x7f8a1c3a in attn_forward kernel_attn.cu:128
  #1 0x7f8a1d22 in run_forward runtime.cu:402
nvml: Xid 79: page fault on device 0
```
maria: also grabbed dmesg lines and nvml output, looks like GPU page fault + segfault right after a batch resize. uploaded artifacts -> s3://redwood-debug/6812345679/logs.tar.gz
sam: did this coincide with the quant-swap rollout? @deploy-bot when was full traffic switch?
deploy-bot: quant-swap-v2 reached 50% at 14:50:12, paused ramp at 15:00:00 due to health checks. no full switch.
ali: okay pause happened. we should consider rolling back to previous quant runtime for us-west-2. any immediate mitigation besides rollback?
casey: reproducer on a dev node: long streaming requests with ~80k token context + burst qps triggers batch resize -> OOM -> segfault. repro steps:
```
# stress script (simple):
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"'$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..65000})'"}' \
    https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate &
done
```
casey: dev node hit cudaErrorMemoryAllocation during dynamic batch growth at ~10 concurrent streams. stack shows kernel attn.cu.
devon: immediate fallbacks we can do: 1) route heavy-context customers to fallback smaller model (gpt-medium) 2) disable kv-prefetch on worker pool 3) lower max_batch_size and max_tokens_for_batching 4) scale up dedicated worker pool temporarily.
lisa: I'll open a rollback PR for quant-swap-v2 to revert us-west-2 to last stable runtime and push HPA bump for the worker pool. starting now.
maria: saved core dump and gdb output to s3: s3://redwood-debug/6812345679/core-and-gdb.tar.gz (contains gdb bt and info proc mappings).
ali: CS update drafted: "We're investigating upstream worker crashes causing 503s, temporary mitigations being applied; ETA 2h, will update." sending now.
sam: tagging oncall infra to check node-level nv drivers and any kernel dmesg: @devon can you run `kubectl describe pod` + `kubectl get events` on affected nodes and check driver versions?
devon: on it. preliminary check: nodes show nvidia-driver 525.85, no kernel rebuilds. one node reports nv_peer_mem warnings at 15:02. collecting `nvidia-smi -q` and nvml logs.
casey: additional note: we saw similar SIGSEGV patterns in a previous quant swap test where fused attention kernel miscompiled on sm86 with certain flags. compile flags changed in v2. worth checking kernel selection.
lisa: rolling back now -> initiating canary rollback to previous runtime for 25% of traffic, will monitor error rate.
incident-bot: Incident created: IN-2026-0318-07 (priority: P1). paging SRE.
ali: immediate action items: (1) rollback quant-swap to previous runtime in us-west-2 (lisa) (2) route heavy-context customers to fallback model (devon) (3) collect core+nvml+dmesg (maria) (4) update CS (ali/sam).
maria: uploaded all artifacts, left notes in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/IN-2026-0318-07
sam: CS notified: two customers acknowledged rerouting, one requested temporary quota increase while we stabilize.
ali: good. keep short updates here. once rollback stabilizes we will scope a deeper postmortem and repro matrix. :thumbsup:
